{{short description|Romanian mathematician}}
{{for|the neurologist|Gheorghe Marinescu}}
[[File:George Marinescu Oberwolfach 2022.jpg|thumb|Marinescu at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2022]]
'''George Marinescu''' (born 22 June 1965, [[Brașov]]) is a Romanian mathematician, specializing in [[complex geometry]], [[global analysis]], and [[spectral theory]].

Marinescu received from the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1988 his baccalaureate degree and in 1989 his master's degree.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=George Marinescu|website=Universität zu Köln|url=http://www.mi.uni-koeln.de/~gmarines/Main1.html}} (short CV & arXiv preprints)</ref> He graduated in 1994 with Ph.D. from [[Paris Diderot University]] (University of Paris 7) with thesis under the supervision of [[Louis Boutet de Monvel]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=105187}}</ref> Marinescu was a postdoc from 1997 to 1998 at the [[University of Edinburgh]], from 1998 to 1999 at the [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu]], and from 1999 to 2000 at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], completing there his [[habilitation]] qualification in 2005. He was at the Humboldt University of Berlin an assistant researcher from 2000 to 2005 and is since 2006 a professor at the [[University of Cologne]].<ref name=CV/>

He was awarded, jointly with [[Xiaonan Ma]], the [[Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer]] Prize in 2006 for their book "Holomorphic Morse inequalities and Bergman kernels".<ref name="Fundació Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer">{{cite web | title=The Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize | website=Fundació Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer | url=http://ffsb.espais.iec.cat/en/the-ferran-sunyer-i-balaguer-prize/ }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v9WnaYHsG1UC|title = Holomorphic Morse Inequalities and Bergman Kernels|isbn = 9783764381158|last1 = Ma|first1 = Xiaonan|last2 = Marinescu|first2 = George|publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag|date = 2007-12-14}}</ref><ref name="Zelditch2008">{{cite journal|last1=Zelditch|first1=Steven|authorlink=Steve Zelditch|title=Book Review: ''Holomorphic Morse inequalities and Bergman kernels''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=46|issue=2|year=2008|pages=349–361|issn=0273-0979|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-08-01224-X|doi-access=free}}</ref> Marinescu was awarded the [[Romanian Academy]]'s 2012 [[Simion Stoilow Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://acad.ro/premiileAR/liste/2012.pdf|title=Premiile Academiei Române pentru anul 2012}}</ref> (with the formal ceremony in 2014).

His son is the scholar of ancient philosophy, Rareș I. Marinescu.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.classics.utoronto.ca/people/directories/postdoctoral-fellows/rare%C8%99-ilie-marinescu|title=Rareș Ilie Marinescu}}</ref>
